text.text_excerpt: I've never had the boiled seafood here but it looks and smells incredible. During crawfish season there are incredibly long lines, so they must be doing something right. I've only had the poboys here and they're pretty delicious. They use Leidenhemer's bread and do not skimp on ingredients. The shrimp poboy is is always filled to the brim with shrimp. The place clearly fries the shrimp to order and has a great breading that doesn't get too soggy after awhile. Generous portion sizes, too!

I kind of swear by Adams Street Grocery po boys, because you can get decent po boys for very cheap. But I had a friend in town and we were planning on getting po boys for dinner, and Adams Street isn't open for dinner, so I was thinking Parkway. But K told me to check out Cajun Seafood, especially if we are getting seafood po boys. I decided to listen to my wise boyfriend who is allergic to all shellfish and give this place a try. Lol. My friend J and I walk in and even though it was really early for dinner on a Sunday the place was quite busy. Maybe everyone was trying to grab some food and go back to their houses and watch football. There were two lines--boiled seafood and fresh seafood...

I love coming home back to the city because I always go to Cajuns to get some crawfish and a hot sausage poboy! Nothing compares. I was so sad to leave because I knew I wasn't going to be able to find food like this in Dallas. The first time I came was on Saturday around lunch time. And we got 6 pounds of crawfish with 2 big shots. Then later on that day we got 2 more pounds of crawfish lol. Yeah, we had been craving some good crawfish so we had to double back. And finally, right before we left to come back to Dallas we got hot sausage poboys, 2 more big shots, and a box of mama noodles. Yes, you can say it was a pretty good experience. I'm just counting the days I can come back home and ...
